problem.heading:
Know where water is rising.
Understand what changed.
problem.intro: Bring a level or pressure exception together with the operating conditions that explain what to inspect next.

cards.title: Rising water between visits
cards.body: A chamber, tank or sump can change while the site is unattended. Select measurement and reporting times around the rate of rise and the response the team can make.

cards.title: Several causes, similar symptoms
cards.body: Rainfall, pumping, downstream surcharge and debris can all influence level. Pressure changes may reflect demand or valve operation. Add the relevant context before labelling a restriction or leak.

cards.title: A command is not an outcome
cards.body: A pump can fail to start or a valve can fail to reach position. Bring run/fault, end-position and measured-flow feedback into the event record before assuming the water system responded.

problem.takeaway: A useful event connects the water asset, measured change, operating context and next inspection.

focus.eyebrow: FROM MEASUREMENT TO A SITE RESPONSE
focus.heading:
Measure the water.
Review the system.
focus.intro: Treat the reading, reference and operating context as one record for the named water asset.

stages.title: Define the operating question
stages.body: Select storage level, suspected restriction, pressure variation or local water ingress as the monitoring task.

stages.title: Choose the sensing arrangement
stages.body: Match radar, immersed level or pressure to the target, liquid, access and exposure.

stages.title: Connect operating evidence
stages.body: Compare rainfall and neighbouring levels with measured flow, pump run/fault and valve position where relevant.

stages.title: Respond and verify
stages.body: Assign inspection or a commissioned remote command; check independent feedback and the resulting water conditions.

focus.note: Level patterns can support a suspected-restriction review. Confirming a blockage, leak location or cause requires additional evidence.
focus.detailTitle: How are level, pressure and flow kept distinct?
focus.detail: Radar measures distance to a suitable target; a known installation reference allows level conversion. An immersed arrangement measures level using its selected sensing principle and reference. A pressure point reports conditions at its process connection. Flow requires an appropriate meter or a validated hydraulic relationship—not a universal conversion from level or pressure. Keep measured and derived quantities identified in the record, with units, timestamps and the assumptions behind any calculation.

steps.title: Review the event
steps.body: Check level, pressure, rainfall, measured flow and current pump or valve feedback.

steps.title: Take the authorised action
steps.body: Assign a field inspection or use a commissioned controller command with the site’s local controls and protection.

steps.title: Check the actual result
steps.body: Confirm run/fault or end-position feedback and the resulting level or flow; retain the completed action.

platform.channels: Choose 4G / NB-IoT for suitable network coverage or LoRa through a compatible gateway; test reception with covers and enclosures in their normal position.
platform.boundary: Local high-level protection and access safety remain independent. Select equipment for the atmosphere and exposure; cloud control is not an emergency or overfill safeguard.

faq.q: Which sensors are included in Smart Water Monitoring?
faq.a: Choose radar or immersed level for the observation point and pressure for the relevant pressurised service. Add Hitelecom water-leak sensing at normally dry locations and configured H600 rainfall where it explains the event. A separate suitable flow meter, pump run/fault signal, valve end-position input or high-level contact adds operating evidence. Water-quality instruments are selected only when quality is part of the objective.

faq.q: Does a rising level prove that a pipe is blocked?
faq.a: No. A sustained rise or a suitable upstream/downstream difference can justify a suspected-restriction review. Rainfall, pumping, downstream surcharge and other conditions may produce similar patterns. Compare the available context and confirm the cause through authorised field inspection or another suitable diagnostic method.

faq.q: Can radar measure through a closed metal pipe?
faq.a: The described radar arrangement needs a suitable path to the selected surface or target. Typical points are open chambers, channels and tanks. A fully flooded pressurised pipe needs a different arrangement, such as appropriate pressure or flow instrumentation. Confirm the geometry and task before choosing the sensing method.

faq.q: Can level or pressure be converted directly into flow?
faq.a: Not universally. Flow requires a suitable meter or a hydraulic relationship whose geometry and assumptions are valid for the site. Keep measured level or pressure separate from derived flow and overflow-volume claims. Validate the complete calculation and identify its reference conditions when it is included in the project.

faq.q: Can Hitelecom remotely operate pumps or valves?
faq.a: Yes, as a commissioned control scope using a suitable Hitelecom IoT Controller and compatible plant interfaces. An HD20 output can issue a command through an appropriately rated control circuit; independent inputs should confirm pump run/fault or valve end-position. Define permissions, local/remote priority, response timing and communications-loss behaviour. Retain local overload, dry-running and high-level protection in their designated systems; remote commands do not guarantee overflow prevention.

faq.q: How do underground sites affect the deployment?
faq.a: Check radio coverage with the cover closed, mounting access, maximum water exposure and every component’s limits. Select the measurement and reporting intervals for the rate of change that matters. Hazardous-atmosphere and access requirements must be assessed for the actual installation, with the appropriate equipment and procedures.

faq.q: Why add a separate high-level contact if level is already measured?
faq.a: A continuous level reading provides the operating trend. Where the site protection design requires an independent high-level switch or alarm, bring its status into the record through an approved interface while keeping its local function independent. Two values on the same cloud screen are not, by themselves, an independent protection architecture.
